obligation: DoD cyber incident report: Aircraft Parts contracts
citation: DFARS 252.204-7012(c)(1)(ii), (c)(2), (c)(3); definition of rapidly report in 252.204-7012(a)
trigger: Cyber incident affecting a covered contractor information system or the CDI in it (GCEE projects for Aircraft Parts programs, including Program H)
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery; update as the review continues
notify: DoD at https://dibnet.dod.mil with a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Aircraft Parts prime and subcontracts include the clause
notifying_entity: Aircraft Parts (director of contracts; certificate holders)
clock_starts: Discovery of the cyber incident (252.204-7012(a), (c)); the runbook uses the time the SOC first suspected unauthorized access

obligation: DoD cyber incident report: Engineering Services contracts
trigger: Same incident; Engineering Services projects in the GCEE and the engineer account
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - separate CAGE codes and contracts; one report per division with cross-references
clock_starts: Discovery of the cyber incident (252.204-7012(a), (c)); the runbook uses the time the SOC first suspected unauthorized access

obligation: Cloud service provider incident duties for SYS-D4 tenants
citation: DFARS 252.204-7012(b)(2)(ii)(D) (CSP must comply with paragraphs (c) to (g))
trigger: Attacker accessed two prime customers' CUI tenants in the industry edition
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery, as paragraph (c) requires; coordinate with each tenant so reports match
notify: DoD at https://dibnet.dod.mil (CSP report); each affected tenant
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Defense Software as CSP to contractor tenants
clock_starts: Discovery by the group SOC; the same clock as the division reports

citation: Industry edition tenant agreements (contract); tenants file their own DoD reports under their contracts
trigger: Tenant CUI accessed by an unauthorized party
deadline: Per tenant agreement (72 hours in both affected agreements); earlier is better because each tenant has its own 72-hour DoD clock
notify: Prime A and Prime D security contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

trigger: Same as the DoD reports
deadline: Starts at discovery; results feed the reports and their updates
notify: Internal; results go to DoD in report updates
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - every affected division
notifying_entity: Group SOC director with division liaisons

obligation: Incident report number to the higher-tier contractor
trigger: DoD assigns an incident report number to a subcontract-related report
deadline: As soon as practicable after the report
notify: Primes A to D for affected Aircraft Parts subcontracts; affected primes for Engineering Services subcontracts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - both CUI divisions hold subcontracts
notifying_entity: Aircraft Parts and Engineering Services contracts leads

trigger: Malicious software discovered and isolated in connection with a reported incident
deadline: As instructed; never to the Contracting Officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if malware is found (an adversary-in-the-middle kit may leave none on group systems)

trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident
deadline: At least 90 days from submission of each report, longer if DoD asks
notify: Internal custody (SOC; forensic retainer; cloud provider A)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: DoD access for forensics and damage assessment
trigger: DoD request for information or equipment; Contracting Officer request for damage assessment information
deadline: On request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

trigger: Cyber incident related to the DoD edition cloud service
deadline: Report via DIBNet; preserve images 90 days from the report
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the DoD edition (SYS-D3) was affected. Not affected in this scenario; confirm and record the reasoning
notifying_entity: Defense Software general manager, DoD edition

trigger: Information about actual, probable, or possible espionage at any location of the cleared contractor (a state-sponsored actor taking defense technical data)
deadline: Promptly; initial report may be by phone, followed in writing
notify: Nearest FBI field office; notify DCSA (the CSA) and give it a copy of the written report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Engineering Services is a cleared defense contractor; facility security officers decide with counsel
clock_starts: When the information comes to the contractor's attention

obligation: Cyber incident on unclassified systems (cleared contractor)
trigger: Cyber incident on a non-Federal unclassified system
deadline: In accordance with contract requirements (the DFARS 252.204-7012 reports above)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - no separate report beyond the contract duties

obligation: Cyber incident on a classified system
trigger: Cyber incident on a classified covered information system approved by the CSO
deadline: Immediately
applies_at_this_tier: No - classified systems were not involved

trigger: Empowered Official believes an ITAR violation may have occurred (technical data reached a foreign person)
deadline: Voluntary. Initial notice immediately after discovery; full disclosure within 60 calendar days of the initial notice unless extended (127.12(c))
applies_at_this_tier: Decision by the Aircraft Parts and Engineering Services Empowered Officials with export counsel; theft by an outside attacker may not be a company violation; record the reasoning either way

trigger: Possible EAR violation (commercial part technology in affected projects)
deadline: Voluntary; a deliberate decision not to disclose a significant apparent violation is an aggravating factor
applies_at_this_tier: Decision by the Empowered Officials with export counsel

trigger: Severity 1 incident
deadline: Within 24 hours of declaration
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

trigger: The registrant determines the incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination; delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - publicly traded registrant
clock_starts: Materiality determination, made without unreasonable delay after discovery

trigger: Annual report
deadline: With the Form 10-K
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - describe processes and governance; consider the incident and lessons learned

trigger: Breach of security of personal information (names with Social Security numbers in the test range badging roster) of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred; 15 more days are available for this notice only, if good cause is given in writing to the Department within those 30 days (501.171(3)(a))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 280 Florida employees affected
notifying_entity: Group Chief Privacy Officer with counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred (the 15-day extension does not apply to this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: No - 280 Florida residents (below 500). Recount if the forensic scope grows

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: No - 640 individuals in total

citation: State breach notification statutes (each state where affected individuals reside)
trigger: Personal information of residents of 5 other states (360 employees)
deadline: Varies by state; follow each state's deadline and regulator notice rules
notify: Affected residents; state regulators where required
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - handled generically with Florida as the worked example
notifying_entity: Group Chief Privacy Officer with counsel

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (call the carrier hotline before hiring vendors)
applies_at_this_tier: Contractual

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
trigger: Suspected theft of defense technical data by a state-sponsored actor
deadline: As soon as practical; coordinate with the 117.8(b) FBI report
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any payment to an extortionist
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if extortion occurs. POL-03 4.9 requires board committee, counsel, and insurer approval

citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Discovery of covered telecommunications equipment or services during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; mitigation details within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - not triggered by this incident type

trigger: Classified or controlled information transferred onto a system not authorized for it
deadline: Upon notification or discovery; follow the Contracting Officer's procedures
applies_at_this_tier: No - not triggered
notifying_entity: Defense Software general manager, DoD edition

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports (PROPOSED)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; not a current obligation
